It added one test target. The target paints three canvas fixtures from Rust (a solid fill, an antialiased edge, and glyphs drawn with the document's font context). For each fixture it takes the driver screenshot in both forms, whole and element by id, and in both layout modes, full and incremental. It then checks each answer digest against a committed table of twelve rows. No PNG is committed.
The founder ruled that canvas-only shots must be byte-equal across hosts (F1, option A). So the no-shot cross-OS rule now has a canvas-only exception. A shot that holds document text still differs between linux x86_64 and macOS aarch64.
The capability statement now carries the canvas exception and the measured difference with its witness. It also lists the canvas conditions that were not measured: another SIMD level of the CPU renderer, a scale other than 1.0, and gradient or image content.
The session changed no product symbol, driver verb, argument, answer field, exit status, dependency, config, CI script or committed check, and retired nothing.

body:
The session added one test target to the blitz-tests harness that paints three canvas-only fixtures (a solid fill, an antialiased edge, glyphs drawn with the document's font context) through custom widgets and reads each one's screenshot answer digest, whole and by element, in both layout modes, against one committed table of twelve digest rows.
It measured those twelve rows byte-equal on CI's linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 hosts (CI run green 17/17); no PNG is committed, only digests.
It scoped the capability statement's shot-bytes limit: a shot holding document text still differs between linux x86_64 and macOS aarch64, while a canvas-only shot is held equal on the three hosts, and the statement now lists the unmeasured canvas conditions (another SIMD level, a scale other than 1.0, gradients).
The founder ratified byte-for-byte equality for canvas-only shots; the no-shot cross-OS rules gain a canvas-only exception in test-plan and architecture, not here.
No product symbol, driver verb, argument, carrier, field, refusal cause, session error, exit code, log field, span, env var, port, socket, dependency, CI script or leg changed; nothing retired.

body_fields.what: added (new file) — a committed stand check of the test harness, its custom widgets painting canvas content with the document's font context, reading the driver session's screenshot answer digest against a table of twelve rows
edited — the committed capability statement, its limit on a shot's PNG bytes across OSes and its list of unmeasured conditions

body: Canvas content crosses only as shot pixels: the new check reads canvas content solely through the screenshot answer's digest; confirm the row stands unmoved (the canvas still crosses only as pixels).

The committed statement of the MCP crossing: the capability statement was edited (the shot-bytes limit scoped to shots with document text, the canvas-only exception, unmeasured canvas conditions); any row holding the statement's shot limit text.

Screenshot answer png contract and the shot encoder rows (png encodes a screenshot, png as the shot encoder): the shot's bytes are now stated byte-equal across three hosts for canvas-only content; a row whose why says shot bytes differ by OS.
Screenshot carried in band and screen pixels in band: the new check consumes the in-band screenshot answer's digest; no new carrier.

Committed stand-Counter checks and any row stating a committed check holds no screenshot step or that a shot repeats on one host only: the rule stands, but its reason now holds for page-text shots alone.
Custom widget handed the document's font context: a test widget's fonts hook keeps the document's font context to draw canvas glyphs.
Custom widget painted and pointed in its content box: the fixtures place a canvas at (8, 8, 200, 100) and assert it paints alone with no named node.
Harness turns on blitz-paint's custom-widget feature: the new harness target relies on it; no manifest line moved.
font-embolden tested by a locked fast leg: the digest table is also read green under blitz-paint/font-embolden.
Lint findings hold no page content / lint findings crossing: the fixtures assert no lint finding through the session's lint call.
CI matrix runs every job: the cross-host reading rests on the linux, windows and macOS test jobs of one run; no job or leg changed.
blitz-tests not published and the test harness taking no tracing and no style: the new target lives in that unpublished harness, adds no dependency and prints nothing.
Locked builds: every gate of the session ran with --locked; no Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock line moved.
Authentication and authorization, CI tokens and publish secrets: no credential, token or publish job was reached.
Secret management and environment variables: no env var read or added.
Outbound network, fetch, CORS, same-origin, navigation and request limits: no network path was reached.
Driver verbs, argument kinds, refusal causes, session errors, exit codes and the session socket or MCP wire grammar: none moved.
Select lists, form controls, masking of password and file values, stable element id and snapshot text: no such behaviour was reached.
Logging, telemetry sink allowlists and spans: no log field or span added.
Data protection rows on history, cookies, HTTP cache, TLS and kept check files: no stored data or kept check moved.
Dependency audit, advisory ignores, licence gate and dependency pins: no dependency added or bumped.

The session measured a canvas shot's bytes on CI's linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 hosts and found them byte-equal, all twelve digest rows held on the three hosts (CI run green 17/17).
It added one integration test target, a stand check of canvas shots: three fixtures (a solid fill, an antialiased edge, glyphs painted on a canvas with the document's font), each painting a canvas alone, read in two shot forms (whole screen and element) in both layout modes, against one table of twelve answer digests written as literals; no PNG is committed.
It edited the capability statement: the limit that a shot's PNG bytes differ between linux x86_64 and macOS aarch64 now holds for a shot holding document text only, a canvas-only shot being held equal on the three hosts; the statement names the canvas conditions left unmeasured.
The founder's ruling F1 (require byte equality) is the ratification the canvas-only exception lands on; no capability is claimed, no product symbol, verb, error, exit, log field, CI job or leg script moved, nothing retired.

the capability statement, its stated limit on a shot's PNG bytes across hosts and its list of unmeasured conditions, read by the capability statement's test in the fast leg

body: decision/cross-os-checks-hold-no-shot: gains the canvas-only exception, a shot holding no document text is byte-equal across linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 and is now compared across hosts by digest; its reason restated to what was measured.

decision/checks-hold-no-screenshot-step and decision/no-screenshot-in-recorded-check-scripts: if their why rests on a shot's bytes differing by OS, that reason is now scoped to a shot holding document text; the rule itself stands.

decision/table-tests-count-their-rows and decision/expected-value-pinned-as-literal: the new digest table asserts its twelve rows and covers every fixture, each expected digest a literal.

decision/requirement-witness-inside-stand-repeat, decision/stand-repeat-three-rounds, decision/zero-failure-stand-repeat and decision/stand-checks-zero-failure-budget: stand-repeat takes the new stand check by its prefix, three of three rounds green.

decision/app-widget-shows-in-shots and contract/handler-coverage-limits/canvas-handler neighbours: canvas widgets painted from Rust are now shot and digested across hosts; the glyph widget keeps the document's font context.

The bundled-font rows (decision/stand-checks-bundled-font, decision/stand-checks-bundled-font-no-skip, decision/stand-pinned-real-font, decision/font-metric-tests-never-skip): the canvas glyph fixture paints through the document's font and never skips.

decision/mutation-controlled-tests: the new check was controlled red-before-green, four controls held.

The screenshot contracts (contract/harness-screenshot/screenshot, contract/harness-screenshot/screenshot-rect, contract/session-run/screenshot, contract/driver-session/screenshot): the whole and element shot forms are now held to a cross-host digest for canvas content; no contract item moved.

decision/test-data-is-code and decision/test-data-in-code: the canvas fixtures and digest table are stated in code, no image or data file committed.

body_fields.fact: Canvas shots are compared across hosts by digest: three fixtures (solid fill, antialiased edge, canvas glyphs), each a canvas alone, in whole and element forms, both layout modes, one table of twelve answer digests, no pixels committed; held byte-equal on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64, ratified by the founder's F1 (require byte equality).

The cross-host equality of a canvas shot is unmeasured under another SIMD level of the CPU renderer, at a scale other than 1.0, or for canvas content beyond the three fixtures; a shot holding document text still differs between linux x86_64 and macOS aarch64.
